name: rajchowk
description: Raj Chowk — Hindi news and political-opinion platform

scripts.typecheck:all: npm run typecheck && npm run typecheck:amplify
scripts.verify: npm run verify:lock && npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck:all && npm run test && npm run build
scripts.verify:full: npm run verify && npm run test:integration && npm run e2e:mocked

scriptsRationale.verify:lock: First step of `verify`, because a package-lock.json that has drifted out of sync with package.json fails `npm ci` in the Amplify backend phase — before any code is compiled — and every other check here would still pass locally against a stale node_modules. That is exactly how a corrupted lock reached main once. `--dry-run` writes nothing. It may reach the registry for metadata, so a fully offline run needs `npm run verify:lock -- --offline`.

overridesRationale.sharp: Next declares optional sharp ^0.34.3, but every 0.34.x inherits four libvips CVEs (GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj). The image optimizer processes user-uploaded avatars, so this is a reachable path. 0.35.x is a semver-minor bump with a stable API. Amplify Hosting supplies its own sharp at runtime; this protects local dev and any self-hosted build.
overridesRationale.postcss: Next pins postcss 8.4.31 internally, which is affected by three sourceMappingURL/stringify advisories. Build-time only and processing our own CSS, but 8.5.x is a semver-minor bump that clears all three.
overridesRationale.notOverridden: immutable@3.7.6 under @ardatan/relay-compiler in the Amplify CLI codegen chain. Fixing it needs a two-major bump that risks breaking ampx, our deployment tool, and it is dev-only tooling that parses our own GraphQL schema — never untrusted input. Tracked in the README security notes.
